label: a6-107-lem-pseudocompact-euclidean-subset-is-closed
tail:
I found no fatal defects in this item. The proof correctly assumes pseudocompactness and non‑closedness, constructs the continuous function \(f(x)=1/\lVert x-p\rVert_2\), shows it is unbounded because \(p\) is a limit point not in \(A\), and obtains a contradiction with the definition of pseudocompactness. The cited dependencies accurately supply the needed facts (closure characterisation, definition of pseudocompact, reverse triangle inequality, and that \(d_2\) is a metric). Any small gaps — such as the implicit fact that open balls are open, that metric continuity coincides with topological continuity, or that the restricted metric gives the subspace topology — are all standard and can be closed by a competent reader in well under thirty seconds; they do not affect the logical validity of the argument. The title matches the statement, and no choice principle beyond a single existential instantiation is used.

Checks performed: contradiction structure, proper use of closure equivalence, unboundedness via open‑neighbourhood argument, continuity estimate (reverse triangle inequality and denominator bounded away from zero), faithful summarisation of dependencies in the Facts block, and absence of hidden hypotheses or misuse of definitions.

0 fatal, 0 nonfatal
